purpose: Machine-readable Organisations & peer community UK v1 metadata extension. It records inspectable geography, leadership, access, moderation and privacy facts without changing the core Resource schema or creating quality or safety scores.

state_semantics.observed: Explicitly published on a reviewed first-party route.
state_semantics.partial: Some relevant information is published but important fields remain unknown.
state_semantics.not_found: Not found on the reviewed public route; this is uncertainty, not evidence that the feature or policy is absent.
state_semantics.not_applicable: The field does not meaningfully apply to this resource type.

geographic_proofs.evidence: BDA Dyslexia Charity Network lists Yorkshire-area association coverage; NAS directory remains a local-search fallback rather than an Oracle-maintained York catalogue.
Dyspraxia Foundation lists a Cumbria local group and BDA network includes regional routes.
ARGH Scotland is Highland-rooted and autistic-led, with Scotland-wide activity.
Disability Wales full-member DPO list includes Accessibility Powys; directory use does not imply neurodivergence-specific support.
Autism NI states support is delivered across Northern Ireland including Fermanagh; PACE peer-network eligibility remains separate.

research_evidence.citation: Crompton CJ, Hallett S, McAuliffe C, Stanfield AC, Fletcher-Watson S. “A Group of Fellow Travellers Who Understand”: Interviews With Autistic People About Post-diagnostic Peer Support in Adulthood. Frontiers in Psychology. 2022;13:831628.
research_evidence.finding: A qualitative UK study of 12 autistic adults found generally positive views of post-diagnostic autistic peer support while also identifying accessibility, facilitator training and support, sustainability, intersectionality and specialist-service boundaries as important design constraints.
research_evidence.limits: Small self-selecting qualitative sample of autistic adults diagnosed in adulthood; it cannot establish universal efficacy, certify any listed group, or generalise to every neurodivergent population.
